steps.text: Heat oil in a deep-fryer or large saucepan to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Whisk flour, wine, water, parsley, garlic, salt, and pepper together in a bowl until well combined and no lumps remain. Dip mushrooms, one at a time, into batter to coat.

Carefully place coated mushrooms into hot oil, making sure they don't touch or stick together while cooking; fry until golden brown, 5 to 6 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate lined. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern-Style Fried Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: Red wine adds an unexpected kick to the batter of these Southern-style fried mushrooms, adding flavor to the crisp coating.

review.reviewBody: I ALMOST rated this 4 stars! Unfortunately as others have noted - you have to add more water. It's not a big deal, true, but if you follow the recipe as written you have a dough and not a batter. It's more like 2 tablespoons. However,the flavor is wonderful and provided you fry it a slightly deep golden brown, provides a nice crispy crunch. I imagine this batter would be great on a lot of vegetables and will try experimenting!

As others have noted, I had to increase the amount of water in this recipe to make it a batter and not a dough. But, other than that, it's great! I even eliminated the oil used in these and opted for my air fryer. It worked well with just a bit of spray in there to get them crispy.

The concept is great! We love breaded mushrooms and these had great taste and presentation. I usually just use pancake batter and didn't have red wine, so I used white cooking wine and a little water in my Member's Mark buttermilk pancake batter. Sprinkled in some Paula Dean's house seasoning and coated sliced fresh white mushrooms with the batter. Fried crispy brown and had a really special flavor. Thanks for sharing you're flavorful and ultra easy idea!

I used this recipe, fried onions, fried pickles and fried nushrooms. Had no parsley so I added 21 seasoning salute from Trader Joe's, added pale ale beer because the batter was too thick and added sherry wine instead of the red wine. Overall it was awesome. Trying to post picture....Thx!

Crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside. Followed recipe except subbed Old Bay seasoning for the Kosher salt and just gave them a shallow fry, turning once during cooking. Drained on wire rack. The wine really gives it nice flavor. Will make again.

I made this as directed, but it looked so thick when I was done mixing the batter that I added some more wine, and some beer. I also just used small whole portabella mushrooms, rather than quartering them and they were fabulous- crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside- will definitely make again!! So Good!!
I had to add extra water & they needed to be fried longer. Great flavor though!

I've never had fried mushrooms before but I saw this recipe and had to try it! It was absolutely delicious. Like everyone said, I did have to add a bit more water to the recipe, and i didn't have any red wine on hand so I substituted diluted red wine vinegar and it was yumyumyum!

Delicious! I made these for my family after a long day of peeling off wallpaper and they were VERY well-received. The wine adds a really nice complexity and they really do cook through in about 5 minutes. I did end up adding more water to the batter and left out the Parmesan cheese because it didn't fit with the rest of my menu. If you want to take these even further, serve them with a creamy dipping sauce: sour cream, cream cheese (or mascarpone), chopped garlic, chopped parsley, minced shallot, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Heaven!
The red wine was a nice touch, but as many others stated liquid amount is off.

I added a 1/2 cup water to make this a batter rather then a dough. I added garlic pepper because I was out of garlic. Oh my goodness no more $8.00 for 8 mushrooms for me. I'll be making these at home from now on. Great with Artichoke and spinach dip. Very very good!

This was the first time I have made fried mushrooms….they were perfect! I did add more water to get the batter consistency I wanted; but the batter was crisp, flaky and very flavorful. Excellent recipe; will make again and again.
Very good just add a little mire wine or water

My daughter and I are eating these as fast as I can make them! We are both big fans of fried morel mushrooms in the springtime, but since we aren't getting them now, we have to settle for fried button mushrooms. I have never made them before, so this is the first recipe I've tried. I picked a good one! These are so good! The parmesan cheese definitely adds just the right flavor they need. You do need to add more water than the recipe calls for to make a batter, but that's an easy fix.
Loved it. As others said it needed more water but I used wine. These were great. Batter is perfect and would be good for other vegi's as well.
Didn't get as crispy as I would have liked. But they tasted good. But didn't get very brown.
I'd stick with a panco style these turn soggy before they have time to even be edible.
This was not a batter for mushrooms. It was too dry, and then with adding in the extra water that others recommended, the batter wouldn't stick to the mushrooms.
This recipe was awesome! As others stated I had to add more water for a batter. But will definitely be making these again.
Great. I saved it. I wonder if the original poster can edit the water amount needed.
